catalog_quote: Our observations agree with those of Jakobi, namely that the underlying system contains two contrastive tones, L and H. (The third tone which Jernudd has heard may be the surface realisation of a downstepped H tone.) There are also various falling and rising contour tones, which can be seen as LH, HL, and H!H sequences on one short or long syllable. Sequences of L, H, LH and HL tones alternate and there is hardly any downdrift. However, there is downstep in certain morphotonological environments which are beyond the scope of this article. With respect to tone-bearing units: short syllables (both open and closed: (C)V(C) can be said to consist of one mora and can contain a maximum of two tones; long syllables (both open and closed: (C)VV(C) consist of two morae and can carry up to three tones on the surface.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Fur is described as a two-tone (H, L) language with the mora as tone-bearing unit, contour tones as tone sequences, lexical and grammatical tone and morphotonological downstep; the description (25 pp., the fullest open phonology of Fur) contains no statement about word stress or accent at all. Tucker & Bryan 1966 (snippet) likewise: 'Tone and Stress: There is little information.'
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; the article notes downstep in certain morphotonological environments and toneless plural suffixes whose tone spreads from the preceding mora.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical words (c. 1000 nouns/adjectives in citation form) plus some verb paradigms for grammatical tone; no phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Kutsch Lojenga & Waag 2004 describe Fur [pɔɔr] as spoken by Darfur speakers (data collected 2002-2003 with four named speakers); no dialect specified. Glottocode furr1244 = ISO fvr; older literature calls the language Kondjara (Meinhof 1917/18) or For (Jernudd 1983, Bender 1996). Bender notes an undescribed variety 'Mimi/Amdang' (Biltine) sometimes grouped with Fur -- that is a separate Glottolog language (amda1238), not covered here.

new_statements.quote: Fur is a register tone language with two tones L and H. Contours on LH and HL are possible. 2. Tone makes lexical distinctions in Fur as exemplified by examples such as: 'desert' úrì 'sheep' úri 3. Tone also functions in the grammar of Fur. Tone is used to differentiate the nominative and locative forms of nouns and the attributive and predicate forms of adjectives.

new_statements.identity_note: All works describe Fur of Darfur (furr1244). Tucker & Bryan 1966 base the Fur sketch on Meinhof's 1917/18 'Kondjara' (= Fur) material; Kutsch Lojenga & Waag 2004 describe Fur of Dar Fur province, Western Sudan (speakers' name [poor]); Noel 2008 elicited from a single native speaker resident in Arlington, Texas. No sub-dialect is specified by any of them.

sources.note: Read in full (syllable/word structure sec.2, consonants, vowels, sec.5 Tone pp.18-24, alphabet). Fur is analysed as a tone language with two underlying tones L and H, contour tones as sequences, mora = TBU, lexical and grammatical tone, downstep. The words 'stress'/'accent'/'prominence' do not occur as prosodic notions anywhere in the article (only 'accents' = diacritics inside the Beaton 1968:2 quotation, and 'acute accent' as the H-tone mark). No statement on word stress.
